root_cause.text: The vulnerability is caused by an off-by-one error in the `hvc_iucv_get_private` function where the bounds check uses `>` instead of `>=`, permitting out-of-bounds access to the `hvc_iucv_table` array when `hvc_iucv_devices` equals the maximum limit of 8.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the modification of the condition from `if (num > hvc_iucv_devices)` to `if (num >= hvc_iucv_devices)` in `drivers/tty/hvc/hvc_iucv.c`, and the CVE description explicitly states that with `MAX_HVC_IUCV_LINES` set to 8, the original check allowed `num` to reach 8, resulting in access to `hvc_iucv_table[8]` which exceeds the valid index range of 0–7.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fixes an off-by-one error in the bounds check to prevent out-of-bounds array access.
intent_record.what: Changed the comparison operator in the bounds check condition from '>' to '>=' inside the hvc_iucv_get_private function.
intent_record.how: Prevents accessing hvc_iucv_table with an index equal to the device count, thereby avoiding out-of-bounds memory access.

vuln_statements.explanation: This bounds check in hvc_iucv_get_private uses '>' instead of '>=', allowing num=8 (equal to HVC_IUCV_MAX_DEVICES) to pass the check and subsequently access hvc_iucv_table[8] which is out-of-bounds since valid indices are 0-7. This off-by-one error permits the out-of-bounds array access described in the root cause.
